title: ES6 Classes
concept: The class syntax is syntactic sugar over prototype-based inheritance — it works the same way internally

steps.title: Defining the Animal class
steps.explanation:
The `class` keyword is syntactic sugar that sets up a constructor function and prototype in one go.
The `constructor` becomes the constructor function, and methods like `eat` are added to `Animal.prototype`.
steps.keyInsight: class = syntactic sugar for constructor function + prototype

steps.title: Dog class inheriting from Animal
steps.explanation: The `extends` keyword automatically sets `Dog.prototype`'s prototype to `Animal.prototype`, creating the inheritance chain.

steps.title: Calling super()
steps.explanation:
In a child class `constructor`, you must call `super()` to run the parent's `constructor`.
This initializes `this.name`.
You cannot use `this` before calling `super()`.
steps.keyInsight: super() = calling the parent constructor (initializes this)

steps.title: Creating an instance
steps.explanation:
Creating the `buddy` instance with `new Dog()`.
`super('Buddy')` is called to set `name`, and `this.breed` is set to 'Golden'.
`buddy`'s prototype points to `Dog.prototype`.

steps.title: Accessing its own property
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.name`.
The property exists directly on `buddy`, so 'Buddy' is returned immediately.

steps.title: Calling a parent prototype method
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.eat()`.
Not found on `buddy` or `Dog.prototype`, so the chain is traversed and `eat` is found on `Animal.prototype`.

steps.title: Calling a child prototype method
steps.explanation:
Looking up `buddy.bark()`.
Not on `buddy` itself, but `bark` is found on `Dog.prototype`.

quiz.question: What is a difference between class syntax and constructor functions?
options: class can be called without new
quiz.explanation:
class is subject to the TDZ, so it can't be used before its declaration.
Calling it without new throws a TypeError.
Methods are non-enumerable.
Internally it still uses prototype.

misconceptions.wrong: JavaScript classes work the same as classes in other languages
misconceptions.correct:
JavaScript class is prototype-based.
It works differently from class-based inheritance in C++ or Java.
misconceptions.why: The syntax looks similar, but internally it still operates through the prototype chain.

keyTakeaway: class = syntactic sugar for prototype inheritance, extends = sets up the chain, super = calls the parent
